_meta.note: Completed 2026-08-22 (fix/date-integrity-monitoring): the original 7-entry file admitted moon-sighting holidays were missing. Non-lunar dates (Language Day, Independence Day, May Day, National Mourning Day, Victory Day, Christmas, July Mass Uprising Day) are gazetted and high-confidence. Lunar/moon-sighting dates (Shab-e-Barat, Shab-e-Qadr/Laylat al-Qadr, Eid-ul-Fitr, Eid-ul-Adha, Ashura, Eid-e-Miladunnabi) are the OFFICIALLY ANNOUNCED government dates as reported in confirmed news (see sources below) -- actual moon-sighting can shift a lunar date by ±1 day in reality, which this file cannot capture in advance. Durga Puja / Vijaya Dashami / Janmashtami (Hindu lunar calendar) are similarly announced-calendar dates, not independently re-derived. IMPORTANT: is_bd_trading_day() gaps in this list are HARMLESS by design -- scrapers/dse_market.py (PR fix/date-integrity-monitoring) now stamps snapshots with the source page's own parsed trading date and gates on already-ingested, not on this calendar; a missing or wrong holiday here at worst causes a same-day-already-ingested no-op (see AGENTS.md landmine 33 cross-reference) rather than a silently dropped or misdated trading day. Two entries (2026-07-01, 2026-12-31, both labelled 'Bank Holiday') are sourced from a single secondary aggregator (calendarlabs.com) curated specifically as DSE market holidays, not independently confirmed via a DSE/BSEC circular or news article -- kept because calendarlabs was directionally correct on every OTHER date this file cross-checked against primary news reporting, but flagged here as the two lowest-confidence entries.
sources: https://www.tbsnews.net/economy/stocks/seven-day-eid-break-dse-stay-closed-17-23-march-1383071 (DSE closed 17-23 March 2026 inclusive for Eid-ul-Fitr/Shab-e-Qadr, incl. the govt-declared extra holiday on 18 March; resumes 24 March)

https://www.tbsnews.net/economy/stocks/dse-remain-closed-august-5-july-mass-uprising-day-1199886 (DSE/CSE closed 5 August 2026 for July Mass Uprising Day, a standing national holiday since 2025)
